parts.given_text: The sample contains 0.750 mol of helium. Its fixed volume is 2.0 × 10⁻² m³ (rounded), initially at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa; the final pressure is 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa. Treat it as a monatomic ideal gas.

sup-5eeff812eafebfb5-q1:whole.hint: Identify what stays fixed: amount of gas, temperature, pressure or volume. Use only the simplification that those conditions allow.
notes: Use pV = nRT = NkT with absolute pressure and kelvin temperature. For a fixed amount, p₁V₁/T₁ = p₂V₂/T₂.
If gas leaks or moves between containers, the amount in one container may change. Apply conservation of total molecules to the complete closed system instead of assuming pV/T is fixed locally.

sup-5eeff812eafebfb5-q2:whole.hint: Link the macroscopic quantity to the random motion and wall collisions of the molecules.
notes: Mean translational kinetic energy is 3kT/2 per molecule. The rms speed obeys v_rms = √(3kT/m), so molecular mass matters when comparing gases.
Pressure comes from the rate of momentum transfer to container walls. In the ideal model, particles have negligible volume and negligible interactions except during elastic collisions.

sup-5eeff812eafebfb5-q4:whole.hint: Write the ideal-gas equation in a form involving mass per unit volume.
notes: Using n = m/M and ρ = m/V gives p = ρRT/M. Keep molar mass M in kg mol⁻¹ when using SI units.
For the same gas, temperature is proportional to p/ρ. Track both changing quantities before deciding how temperature changes.
